verdict.headline: The leveraged position is closed.
verdict.detail: The leveraged position is closed. Georg instant-sold Gruber to Kickbase this morning at exactly market value, took the matchday bonus alongside it, and the balance went from deeply negative to positive with the figures reconciling to the cent. The matchday-zero risk that dominated the last several runs is gone, more than a day and a half before the lock. What it cost is a body: the squad now sits at exactly eleven, four-four-two is the only legal formation, every player is fielded and there is no bench. That single fact drives everything below. With no twelfth man, a sale costs the ten-player penalty, so each buy permits exactly one sale and every purchase has to be a same-position swap funded by the man it replaces plus the small cash balance. No points trade clears that test this run. The one action worth taking is the flip, and its clock is short.

sell.reason: Nothing. This is a deliberate no, not an omission. The standing sell call on Gregoritsch is closed unexecuted and that is the correct outcome rather than a miss — it was always the fallback unwind leg and explicitly mutually exclusive with the Gruber leg. The Gruber leg fired, so executing this one on top of it would drop the squad to ten and cost the penalty, which is exactly what the mutual-exclusivity guard was written to prevent. No future run should resurrect it to fund anything while the squad sits at eleven. Neuer cannot be sold either, on a harder constraint than merit: he is the only keeper and every formation requires one, so selling him is forbidden rather than merely unwise until a replacement has actually landed.

buy.reason: Nothing clears, and the misses are narrow enough to be worth naming so the next run does not re-derive them. Banzuzi is the real one — a large upgrade on Tanaka in the same midfield slot, a board listing priced at market value with a rising flag, and his auction resolves before tonight's tick — but selling Tanaka plus the cash balance falls short of his price, and closing that gap means a second sale into ten players. Krattenmacher fails the same way by a smaller margin and is a far smaller upgrade. Every defender who would actually improve on Deman or ter Horst sits well beyond the largest single-swap budget available. Among the attackers on the board, not one beats either of the two Georg already fields. Padding a position he already covers would be the only way to spend here, and that is not a points trade.
